label: copy-phase input token q
explanation: Fires exactly when the token q is fed back as input during the copy phase (every copy-phase q input, precision 1.0, recall 0.999). Never fires on q in the original phase or at the delimiter, and essentially never on other tokens (the ~0.1% misses are tiny activations on the step just before a q input). Magnitude is fairly uniform (~0.75-1.0 of max). In the examples it was weaker (~0.57-0.63 of max) when the q is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, input right after <DEL>), and somewhat stronger for later repeated q copies. That pattern was read off examples, not measured systematically.

issues: No real problems found. On the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.999, F1 0.9995, mass recall 0.99998, correlation 0.993, and 0 false positives.

The 92 test misses all have the same pattern: a tiny activation (0.01-0.03 of max) on the copy-phase input just before a q input. They hold 0.0% of activation mass. This is a weak early-onset effect, not a separate class of inputs the feature responds to.

The profile backs up the phase claims. There are 0 activations in the original phase and at the delimiter, and the copy phase holds 100% of activation mass. Among input tokens, q holds 1.000 of the mass, and the other tokens (j, i, s, h, n) have at most 25 activations each.

The profile also backs up the claim that the first copied token is weaker, although it was not measured directly. recall_idx 1 has 16560 activations carrying 14.1% of mass, versus 16746 carrying 18.6% at recall_idx 2. That makes the mean activation per firing at the first copy step about 76% of the later steps' level.
